candidate.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on schema mismatch and can crash calendar operations when callers don’t catch it
reports: salesforce's refresh-token schema incorrectly requires scope, which salesforce refresh responses omit, causing valid responses to be rejected.

concurrent getservice() calls race on the credential update; injected parserefreshtokenresponse sync branch returns parse result but sibling branch rejects with new error, inconsistent with httperror usage

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/calendarservice.ts:98 — refresh is a non-atomic read-modify-write of credential.key, so concurrent bookings and the sync webhook can clobber a newer token with a stale one.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/calendarservice.ts:795 — the !accesstokenparsed.success branch is dead because parserefreshtokenresponse throws on failure, and the hardcoded login.salesforce.com breaks sandbox orgs.

parserefreshtokenresponse now unconditionally throws on parse failure, but callers in office365calendar, salesforce, and zoom still branch on success, making the office365 fallback path unreachable and silently changing behavior

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/calendarservice.ts:264 — refresh paths merge an in-memory snapshot of the key captured at construction and write the whole object back (read-modify-write, same in google at calendarservice.ts:97), so a webhook-synced key arriving mid-request is clobbered by the stale merged key from an in-flight refresh. (p2, conf 50)
candidate.example: salesforce's refresh-token schema incorrectly requires scope, which salesforce refresh responses omit, causing valid responses to be rejected.

fix_scope: minimal fix for the demonstrated instance only

sibling_instances.note: other instances of this class are unverified siblings; fix.patch does not address them

claim_restated: parseRefreshTokenResponse should not throw when a provider's refresh-token response fails schema validation (e.g., missing `scope`), and instead return a Zod safeParse result with success:false so callers can handle it without crashing.
expected_failure: parseRefreshTokenResponse should not throw on schema mismatch; it should return { success: false } so callers can branch instead of crashing
